title: Reliability-Aware ETF Tail-Risk Monitoring
summary: This paper by Tenghan Zhong proposes a reliability-aware framework for daily ETF tail-risk surveillance. The framework combines data quality checks at service time, lower-tail prediction, uncertainty scoring, and conservative risk adjustment. It is evaluated on a daily panel of multiple ETFs augmented with VIX and yield-curve data using a rolling walk-forward design. Results suggest the framework improves tail-risk reliability during stressed periods and maintains robustness under deliberate input corruption.
key_points: The framework targets next-day tail-risk surveillance for ETFs and addresses unreliability caused by data quality degradation, market condition shifts, or unstable predictive performance.
Four components are combined: service-time quality checks, lower-tail prediction, uncertainty scoring, and conservative risk adjustment.
Empirical evaluation uses a daily panel of multiple ETFs augmented with VIX and yield-curve information under a rolling walk-forward design.
The system improves tail-risk reliability during stressed market periods while preserving full evaluable coverage.
Under deliberate input corruption, the quality layer is reported to enhance service robustness.
